subject: Request: temporary p95 derating & canary plan for hosted API during migration
messages:
From: Sophie Allen <sophie.allen@cedartech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cedartech.com
Date: 2026-06-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Temporary p95 relaxation request during CedarTech DB migration

Hi Kimberly,

Quick context: CedarTech is doing a cross-region DB migration and cache warmup the week of June 10-12. We expect a combination of cache misses and traffic skew as services rehydrate. Our platform will continue to call Redwood for hosted generation; however, we expect a transient increase in end-to-end tail latency for the /v1/generate route (particularly long-context chat sessions).

Request: would Redwood consider a temporary, scoped p95 derating for our hosted API (specific API key / routes) during the migration window? We are targeting a 72-hour window and would like clarity on how Redwood measures p50/p95 during carveouts and the proposed operational controls (canary, tagging to exclude from contractual SLOs, telemetry).

What we can provide: action plan, times (start/end UTC), brief traffic profile (tokens/minute by route), and a performance snapshot from last week. I've attached our migration plan and a CSV with baseline traffic.

Appreciate a quick read — our ops team needs to confirm fallback behavior for user-facing flows.

Thanks,
Sophie Allen
Head of Platform Ops | CedarTech
(attachment: cedar_migration_action_plan.pdf)
(attachment: performance-snapshot.csv)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Allen <sophie.allen@cedartech.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary p95 relaxation request during CedarTech DB migration

Hi Sophie — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. Short answer: yes, we can support a scoped temporary p95 derating, but we need to lock the operational controls and limits before the window. Proposed approach below.

Proposed carveout and controls
- Scope: applies only to the API key(s) you specify and routes matching /v1/generate and /v1/chat.generate.
- Window: provisional 2026-06-10T00:00:00Z through 2026-06-12T23:59:59Z (UTC).
- Derating: p95 target temporarily relaxed from 400ms to 800ms for affected keys/routes. p50 target remains unchanged.
- Canary: 3-stage canary (5% -> 25% -> full) across the first 18 hours of the window. Canary traffic will be tagged with "cedar-migration" so we can exclude/instrument separately.
- Measurement: Redwood will calculate p50/p95 using the standard rolling 24-hour measurement buckets for customer-facing SLAs, but traffic tagged with "cedar-migration" will be excluded from contractual SLO computations for the 72-hour window. We will maintain a separate report that includes the tagged traffic for transparency.
- Fallbacks: automatic model fallback to a lower-latency model variant and increased batching thresholds during the window. We will log each fallback event and provide an incident summary daily.

What we need from CedarTech
- Confirm the exact API keys and routes to include.
- Provide the confirmed UTC start/end timestamps.
- A short traffic profile by route (tokens/minute typical & peak) and whether the migration will include long-context sessions (>2k tokens).
- Contact for on-call coordination during the window.

We've looped Aditya for SRE capacity planning and Rishi for contractual addendum wording. Once we confirm, we can issue a one-page SLO addendum and a DocuSign link for signature. If you want faster staging verification, we can run a short pre-migration canary next week.

Kimberly Park
Director, Account & Partner Success | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-06-03T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary p95 relaxation request during CedarTech DB migration — SRE notes

Adding a few SRE notes and constraints so expectations are aligned.

Technical notes
- Canary cadence: recommend 5% for first 3 hours, 25% for next 6 hours, then 100% if no unexpected tail events. This gives us early signals on KV-cache misses and sequence-length regressions.
- Measurement exclusion tagging: we'll exclude traffic that contains header X-Redwood-Carveout: cedar-migration from SLA rollups. That means the contractual p95 will be calculated over non-tagged traffic only for the carveout window. We will keep the tagged traffic in a separate monitoring bucket for audit.
- Telemetry: please ensure your client sets the session-length metadata (approx token length) and a correlation id — this helps us surface long-context regressions.
- Capacity: with expected peak tokens/min you provided, we can handle the traffic at 1-1.2x current provisioned capacity but we may need short bursts on dedicated capacity if peak sustains > 15 minutes. If CedarTech cannot accept model fallbacks, we will need a pre-approved temporary quota increase.

Contracts & change control
- Rishi, please confirm whether we need a formal addendum or a short-term amendment.

Next steps
- Sophie: confirm API keys, exact start/end in UTC, and whether fallbacks are acceptable.
- Kimberley: if you approve these SRE notes, I'll draft the internal runbook and schedule a 30-minute readout with CedarTech.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior SRE Manager | Redwood Inference

Sophie —

Thanks for confirming the API keys and the final window (2026-06-10T00:00:00Z to 2026-06-12T23:59:59Z). Redwood is approving the temporary p95 derating under the controls below. Please review and sign the addendum (DocuSign link below) — the carveout will not be active until we have a signed addendum and your production traffic sets the X-Redwood-Carveout header.

Final agreed items
- Scope: API keys ak_live_******** (as provided), routes /v1/generate and /v1/chat.generate only.
- Window: 2026-06-10T00:00:00Z — 2026-06-12T23:59:59Z (UTC).
- Contractual modification: p95 relaxed to 800ms for the window; p50 unchanged.
- Tagging: traffic must include header X-Redwood-Carveout: cedar-migration to be excluded from contractual SLO rollups.
- Canary: 5% (3h) -> 25% (6h) -> 100% remainder. Redwood will run an isolated canary on a staging pool the day prior if you opt in.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to the model variant faster-latency-1 is enabled. If CedarTech opts out of fallback, we will require a temporary quota lift.
- Observability: daily summary emails during the window and final post-mortem within 48 hours. Logs and fallback counts will be attached as CSV.

Attachments: draft SLO addendum included for review (slo-addendum-cedartech.pdf). DocuSign: https://docusign.com/embeddedSigning/abc123. HubSpot: https://na1.hubspot.com/deals/DEAL-87219

When you sign, we'll turn on the carveout and confirm on-call rotations. Appreciate the clear migration plan — this should minimize customer-facing disruption.

Best,
Kimberly Park
